<Heading

  children={"Batch Query Device Matching Capabilities and Current Trait Values"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/devices/capabilities"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Batch-query matching capabilities for the explicit `deviceIds` list. Always returns a device array, with no pagination. `deviceIds` is required, and the raw array may contain at most 20 items, including duplicates. After trimming, devices are queried in first-occurrence order with duplicates removed.
Provide at least one non-empty list among `functionCodes`, `traitCodes`, and `commandCodes`. List items must not be blank, and array elements are not split by commas. Unknown fields and `pageNum`/`pageSize` return `400`.
All devices use the same filter conditions. Matching rules are identical to GET: conditions of different categories are combined with AND, and an `and` match for traits or commands requires all codes to match within the same function.
If only `functionCodes` is provided, the complete traits and commands under each matched function are returned. If leaf conditions are provided, only matched leaves are retained. Passing both `traitCodes` and `commandCodes` requires a function to satisfy both categories at the same time; this is not a union.
If a device is accessible but no capabilities match, the device is retained with `endpoints=[]`. Devices that do not exist or are inaccessible are omitted. If all devices are omitted, `data=[]`. Results are ordered by the first occurrence of each requested ID, with no `hasMore` and no silent truncation.
Current trait values are read from Studio's current control points. They are not refreshed from physical devices, and a simultaneous snapshot across devices is not guaranteed. When available, `value`/`time` are returned. Null-value fields may be omitted, while `false` and `0` are returned normally. Commands have no current value.
Definitions reuse the ordinary `DeviceDefinition` and do not include numeric `functionId`/`traitId`/`commandId`/`fieldId`. The request body is a JSON object directly and is not wrapped in `data`. The request text may contain at most 1 Mi characters.
POST requires separate interface access authorization; GET permission alone does not implicitly grant access. Parameter errors return `400` for the whole batch. Unhandled query exceptions use the unified error response and are not disguised as successful partial results.
